land.text: Zheng's first seat in the royal domain near modern Hua County, Shaanxi, on the Wei River

predecessors.note: Granted out of the royal domain: the Zheng page calls Zheng a 'vassal state' of the Zhou, 'in the royal domain' near Hua County, Shaanxi.

successors.note: 'In 375 BCE during the following Warring States period Zheng was annexed by Han state.' Han moved its capital to Xinzheng.

capitals.name: Zheng (near Hua County, Shaanxi)
capitals.note: The states table: 'Zheng | Hua County, Shaanxi | 806 BCE'. Coordinates are the modern county seat (researcher's reading); the page gives no coordinates.

capitals.name: Xinzheng (Henan)
capitals.note: 'Duke Wu (r. 770-744) moved Zheng state east'; the page dates no move beyond that reign span and lists Xinzheng as the second capital. Han took Xinzheng as its own capital after 375.

rulers.name: Duke Huan (Yǒu 友)
rulers.note: Reign years as the Zheng page's table gives them; the page's chart gives 757-743 for the start of Duke Zhuang, against 743-701 in the table.

correction.text: Zheng at its grant: a small domain near modern Hua County, Shaanxi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Zheng shape begins in 750, but the page puts the founding in 806 in the royal domain near Hua County, Shaanxi, 'on the Wei River'; Zheng reached the Henan plain only under Duke Wu (r. 770-744). The disc is the researcher's reading of 'near Hua County'.

New keyframe: the 750 shape stretched back to Duke Wu's move east in 770. The annexations of Hui and Yan (769), Eastern Guo (767) and Hu (763) in the SA states table fall inside these years and are not located by any page, so the shape is held steady; the 750 shape already contains them.

5,278 km2 for 750-451. The pages give no area to compare. Within these years the SA table dates Ji to 750 and Dai to 713 (both to Zheng) and Zheng's capital stays Xinzheng; the shape is plausible for the Henan plain around Xinzheng (it contains the Zhengzhou cell), unverified beyond that.

10,403 km2 for 450-405, double the earlier shape. Page silent: no page opened explains the doubling; in Cliopatria the 25 new cells are 20 from the last Cao shape and 4 from Cai (both end 451). Kept as drawn; unverified: page budget.
10,227 km2 for 404-384, within 2% of the previous shape. Page silent on any change; kept as drawn.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, valid to 375 BC; years only

keyframe_review.note: 10,125 km2. Cliopatria runs Zheng to 367 but the pages date the annexation by Han to 375 (Zheng infobox 'Disestablished 375 BC, conquest by Han'; states table '375 BCE: to Han'), so the shape is right for 383-376 and Zheng is Han's from 375 (the last Zheng year is 375).

region.text: Zheng's first seat in the royal domain near modern Hua County, Shaanxi, on the Wei River

ledger.note: 806 BC: King Xuan of Zhou grants Zheng, a small domain in the royal domain near Hua County, Shaanxi. 'Zheng was founded in 806 BC when King Xuan of Zhou' (lead); the SA states table: 'Zheng | Hua County, Shaanxi | 806 BCE'. Duke Huan was killed when 'the Quanrong tribes sacked the Zhou capital Haojing in 771 BC'.

770: Duke Wu moves Zheng east. 'Duke Wu (r. 770-744) moved Zheng state east' to Xinzheng, Henan. The page gives no year for the move beyond the reign; the SA table lists Xinzheng as the second capital. After 771 the Zhou court relied on Zheng and Jin.

375: Han conquers Zheng. 'In 375 Han defeated the neighboring state of Zheng' and annexed it, moving its own capital to Xinzheng; the Zheng page: 'In 375 BCE ... Zheng was annexed by Han state.'
375: Zheng ends. Infobox 'Disestablished 375 BC, conquest by Han'; the last duke is Duke Kang (r. 395-375). The land passes to Han.

wars.name: Battle of Xuge
wars.outcome: Zheng defeated the royal forces and injured King Huan: 'Zheng was the first vassal to openly defy the king.'

wars.name: Zheng against Jin, Song, Chen and Wey
wars.outcome: Under Duke Mu Zheng defeated a combined alliance of Jin, Song, Chen and Wey in 607 BCE.
wars.note: No land changed hands on the page.

wars.name: Han conquest of Zheng
wars.outcome: Han annexed Zheng in 375 and made Xinzheng its capital.
wars.note: The war's start is undated on the page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is on any page; the founding seat near Hua County is a point, and the Henan plain frontier with Song, Wey, Chu and Han is approximate throughout.

notes: Zheng (Q197598). Cliopatria begins Zheng in 750 and ends it in 367; the pages give 806 (founding in the royal domain at Hua County, Shaanxi) and 375 (annexation by Han), so two years-only/new keyframes were added and the last shape is shortened. Pages opened: Zheng (state), Spring and Autumn period (states table with the annexations of Hui, Yan, Eastern Guo, Hu, Ji, Dai and the fall of Zheng), Han (Warring States). The 769-713 annexed states are small Western Zhou/Spring and Autumn states without dossiers; they are listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers. Not on any page: the date of the move from Hua County to Xinzheng other than Duke Wu's reign (770-744); the 5th-century doubling of the shape (confidence-1 events cite Cao and Cai because Cliopatria hands those cells over); Zheng's wars with Chu, Jin, Song (undated on the pages). Zheng was a vassal of the Zhou king; any vassal_start belongs to the Zhou dossier. Gazetteer: no new names; Hua County and Xinzheng are by Weinan and Zhengzhou (Xinzheng and Hua County are not in places.jsonl).
